steps.title: Exotic perfume
steps.body: Gewürztraminer gives deep golden wines with intense aromas of lychee, rose petals, ginger, Turkish delight and sometimes smoke. It's full-bodied, low in acidity and high in alcohol, often 13.5 to 14.5%. Even dry versions can seem sweet because of the perfume. Few grapes are easier to recognise.

steps.title: Spicy Traminer
steps.body: Gewürz means spice in German. The grape is an aromatic, pink-skinned mutation of Savagnin, the Traminer family, named after Tramin, or Termeno, in Alto Adige, Italy. Its pink to red skin gives white wines a deep golden colour. It buds early and ripens to high sugar.

steps.prompt: What does Gewürz mean in German?
steps.explanation: Gewürz means spice, for its spicy aromatic character.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for deep gold colour, an explosive nose of lychee and rose, and a full, oily palate with low acidity. A slight bitterness on the finish is common. If you smell lychee, it's almost certainly Gewürztraminer.

steps.prompt: Gewürztraminer usually has very high acidity.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's typically low in acidity, which is why it can feel heavy.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Gewürztraminer smells of lychee, rose and ginger
It's a pink-skinned mutation of the Traminer family from Tramin
It's full-bodied, low in acidity and high in alcohol
